knowledge.display_text: In the 2017 review, Alzheimer disease is the leading worldwide cause of dementia; an estimated 5.4 million Americans are affected, with a projected tripling by 2050 in the absence of breakthroughs.
No disease-modifying therapy for Alzheimer disease had been clinically approved at the time of this 2017 review.
Alzheimer disease has extracellular amyloid-beta plaques and intracellular tau neurofibrillary tangles; plaques are relatively specific to AD, whereas tangles also occur in other disorders.
Sequential beta- and gamma-secretase cleavage of transmembrane APP releases extracellular Aβ peptides, usually 40–42 residues, which aggregate into oligomers, beta-sheet fibrils and plaques.
Some studies suggest amyloid pathology reflects asymptomatic preclinical AD more closely, whereas tau tangles track the onset of clinical symptoms more closely.

Anti-amyloid approaches (gamma-secretase inhibition, active immunotherapy and anti-Aβ antibodies) showed promise in animal models, but most mid-to-late clinical studies missed primary endpoints; a selective tau aggregation inhibitor also missed primary outcomes in mild-to-moderate AD.
Evidence reviewed in 2017 implicates cytokine-mediated neuroinflammation in AD development; TNF-α participates in the inflammatory cytokine cascade and may be a therapeutic target.
TNF-α levels are normally very low in healthy adult peripheral and central systems but are significantly elevated in blood and CNS in AD; clinical and animal studies link excess brain TNF-α to AD.
TNF-α is a nonglycosylated 17-kDa type-II transmembrane monomer in the TNF/TNFR superfamily; membrane homotrimers are cleaved by TNF-α-converting enzyme to soluble 51-kDa trimers.
Brain microglia, neurons and astrocytes can synthesize TNF-α, a cytokine recognized initially for antitumor activity that initiates and propagates inflammation.
TNF-α binds TNFR1 (p55-R) and TNFR2 (p75-R). TNFR1 contains an intracellular death domain, whereas TNFR2 lacks it.
Ubiquitously expressed TNFR1 is activated by soluble or membrane TNF-α; its effects include proliferation, activation, antiviral activity and especially apoptosis and cytotoxicity.

attributes.name: effects
attributes.value: cell proliferation; activation; antiviral activity; apoptosis; cytotoxicity

knowledge.display_text: TNFR2 has higher TNF-α affinity, preferential membrane-TNF activation and low expression mainly in immune/endothelial cells; it can activate cIAP1/2, NF-κB and PI3K-dependent inflammatory and survival pathways.
TNFR2 may indirectly enhance TNFR1-mediated cytotoxicity but does not induce cytotoxicity alone; the general consensus contrasts pro-apoptotic TNFR1 with survival/proliferation-promoting TNFR2.
TNF-α was detected around Aβ plaques in postmortem human AD brains; TNFR1 signaling was required for Aβ-induced neuronal death in subsequent studies.
Compared with nondemented human brains, AD brains had higher TNFR1 and lower TNFR2 protein; TNF-α affinity increased for TNFR1 and decreased for TNFR2.
Genetic association studies implicated chromosome 12p (TNFR1 gene) and chromosome 1p (TNFR2 gene) regions in late-onset Alzheimer disease.
Reported studies found significantly elevated TNF-α in CSF and serum of AD patients, with TNF-α elevation correlated with disease progression.

conditions: Reported clinical studies; CSF and serum, not automatically plasma

knowledge.display_text: AD transgenic mice had elevated brain TNF-α, associated with intraneuronal Aβ immunoreactivity in entorhinal cortex and correlated cognitive deficits.
Deleting TNFR1 in AD transgenic mice reduced Aβ formation/plaque burden, BACE1 expression and cognitive deficits; genetic TNFR1 signaling inactivation prevented intraneuronal Aβ accumulation.

attributes.name: outcomes
attributes.value: reduced Aβ formation; plaque burden; BACE1 expression; cognitive deficits; prevented intraneuronal Aβ accumulation

knowledge.display_text: Deleting TNFR2 worsened pathology in an AD mouse model; deleting both TNFR1 and TNFR2 exacerbated Aβ/tau pathology, which the review attributes to losing TNFR2 protection.

attributes.name: author_explanation
attributes.value: aggravation of TNFR1-mediated pathology resulting from silencing TNFR2

knowledge.display_text: In mouse AD models TNF-α increased Aβ production through beta-secretase expression and gamma-secretase activity; chronic neuronal TNF-α expression caused extensive neuronal death.

attributes.name: mechanism
attributes.value: upregulated beta-secretase expression and gamma-secretase activity

knowledge.display_text: Excess brain TNF-α may enhance Aβ production, inhibit microglial Aβ clearance, cause synaptic dysfunction and neuronal loss, and accelerate cognitive decline; these processes implicate TNF-α across AD stages.

conditions: Figure 1 and reviewed studies; not proof of human treatment efficacy

attributes.name: processes
attributes.value: increased Aβ production; decreased microglial clearance; synaptic dysfunction; neuronal loss; cell death; accelerated progression and cognitive decline

knowledge.display_text: FDA-approved biologic TNF inhibitors treat peripheral inflammatory diseases (Crohn disease, rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis); examples are infliximab, adalimumab, golimumab, certolizumab and etanercept.

attributes.name: indications
attributes.value: Crohn disease; rheumatoid arthritis; psoriatic arthritis

knowledge.display_text: TNF-specific antibodies and etanercept bind soluble and membrane TNF-α and prevent signaling through both receptors; etanercept fuses the TNFR2 extracellular domain to human IgG1 Fc.

attributes.name: etanercept_structure
attributes.value: TNFR2 extracellular domain fused to the c-terminal of human IgG1 Fc

knowledge.display_text: Intrahippocampal/intracerebral delivery of recombinant dominant-negative TNF inhibitor in AD transgenic mice inhibited soluble-TNF signaling and reduced preplaque Aβ pathology.

knowledge.display_text: Intracerebroventricular infliximab in mouse AD models reduced TNF-α, amyloid plaques, tau phosphorylation and cognitive deficits.
A small open-label six-month study reported improved ADAS-Cog, Severe Impairment Battery and MMSE after perispinal etanercept 25–50 mg/week in AD patients.

conditions: Small open-label human study; no controlled efficacy conclusion

knowledge.display_text: Rapid CSF penetration and nonsynaptic signaling were hypothesized explanations for perispinal etanercept improvement; another study found perispinal accumulation without consistent intracranial delivery.

conditions: Separate studies; hypothesis is not established delivery

knowledge.display_text: Larger controlled trials are needed to confirm the encouraging small perispinal/open-label and intrathecal case findings for biologic TNF inhibitors in AD.

conditions: Larger controlled trials; current findings are not confirmation

knowledge.display_text: Approved biologic TNF inhibitors have limited BBB penetration, and invasive delivery may be unsafe or impractical for chronic AD dosing.

statements.modality: limited penetration; invasive routes may be unsafe or impractical

knowledge.display_text: Peripheral TNF modulation showed promise in transgenic mice, but a small randomized double-blind phase-II trial of weekly subcutaneous etanercept in mild-to-moderate AD found no improvement in cognition, global function or behavior.
Further studies must determine whether modulating peripheral TNF-α improves clinical AD outcomes and how it affects AD pathology.

A BBB molecular Trojan horse is an endogenous peptide or peptidomimetic antibody transported through endogenous receptors such as transferrin or insulin receptors, ferrying an attached biologic into brain.

Engineer a mouse-targeted cTfRMAb-TNFR fusion by joining the TNFR2 extracellular-domain amino terminus to the chimeric transferrin-receptor antibody heavy-chain carboxyl terminus; this leaves the TfR-binding terminus free and TNFR dimeric.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.value: TNFR2 ECD amino terminus to heavy-chain carboxyl terminus

attributes.name: configuration
attributes.value: TNFR ECD dimer; cTfRMAb amino terminus available

knowledge.display_text: Human and mouse monomeric TNF-α have high amino-acid identity; human TNFR binds mouse TNF-α with high affinity, supporting use of human TNFR in the mouse fusion.

attributes.name: sequence_identity
attributes.value: high human–mouse monomeric TNF-alpha amino acid identity

knowledge.display_text: The cTfRMAb-TNFR fusion binds mouse TfR with Kd 2.6±0.3 nM and TNF-α with Kd 96±34 pM.
The bifunctional mouse fusion permits rapid noninvasive transvascular delivery through TfR-mediated transcytosis and, once in brain, sequestration of excess TNF-α.
Pharmacokinetic analysis found intraperitoneal, subcutaneous and intravenous cTfRMAb-TNFR delivery produced brain fusion concentrations 20–50 times pathological brain TNF-α concentrations.
Intravenous delivery is preferred for acute neurological conditions such as ischemic stroke; intraperitoneal/subcutaneous routes are considered more practical for chronic conditions including AD.
The cTfRMAb-TNFR fusion was protective in mouse ischemic-stroke and Parkinson-disease models; its evaluation in an AD mouse model was ongoing.

For potential human use, investigators engineered HIRMAb-TNFR by fusing TNFR2 extracellular domain to a chimeric/humanized human-insulin-receptor antibody; HIRMAb cross-reacts with Old World primate insulin receptors.

attributes.name: author_characterization
attributes.value: HIRMAb described as the most potent engineered molecular Trojan horse for human brain

knowledge.display_text: In rhesus monkeys, an intravenous 0.2-mg/kg HIRMAb-TNFR dose yielded brain uptake 3±0.1% injected dose/100g brain versus 0.23±0.06% for TNFR:Fc.
Chronic high-dose administration of a HIRMAb-based fusion protein (20 mg/kg) was reported safe in rhesus monkeys; this is not established safety of AD treatment in humans.

conditions: Chronic primate administration; not a human AD clinical safety study

knowledge.display_text: TNF-α inhibition is a potential AD strategy: clinical and animal evidence motivates it, but BBB delivery and controlled human efficacy remain limitations; molecular Trojan horses may offer noninvasive peripheral-and-brain targeting.
Investigators tested the engineered cTfRMAb-TNFR fusion in mouse neurological models and characterized systemic pharmacokinetics.

conditions: Reported completed preclinical tests; AD-model investigation still ongoing

knowledge.display_text: Measure brain uptake after intravenous fusion-protein dosing in rhesus monkeys and evaluate chronic high-dose HIRMAb-based administration.

conditions: Reported primate experiments, not human AD treatment

knowledge.display_text: A reported open-label clinical study administered perispinal etanercept for six months and assessed cognition in AD patients.
A reported randomized double-blind phase-II human trial tested weekly subcutaneous etanercept for cognition, global function and behavior in mild-to-moderate AD.
